questions.question: What is the difference between an Angular component and a module, and how do they relate?
questions.title: Angular Components vs Modules
questions.direct_answer: A component is a reusable UI building block — a TypeScript class + template + styles that controls a patch of the screen. A module (NgModule) is an organizing container that groups related components, directives, and services and configures the DI compiler. Components are the bricks; modules are the boxes that group bricks and declare which bricks belong together. Every Angular app has at least a root module (AppModule) that bootstraps the app, and a root component (AppComponent) that hosts the view.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you understand components as UI units and modules as organizational/DI containers — and that a module declares and groups components rather than rendering anything itself.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking a module 'is a bigger component' or that modules render UI — modules organize; components render.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: A component is a UI unit (class+template+styles); a module is a container that groups components/directives/services and wires DI. Components render; modules organize.

sections.title: Components Render, Modules Organize
sections.content: A component is a reusable piece of UI: a TypeScript class decorated with @Component that pairs with an HTML template and styles to control a patch of the screen. A module (NgModule) is an organizational container decorated with @NgModule that groups related components, directives, and services, and tells Angular's compiler how to wire dependency injection. The key distinction: components render UI; modules don't render anything — they organize and configure. Every app has a root module (AppModule) that bootstraps, and a root component (AppComponent) that hosts the view tree.

sections.title: Component vs Module
sections.content:
A component is a UI unit; a module groups UI units and services.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  M[AppModule: organizes] --> C1[AppComponent: renders]
  C1 --> C2[Child components: render]
  M -.declares.-> C1 & C2
  M -.provides.-> S[Services for DI]
```

sections.title: A component and a module side by side
Common Mistakes
items: Thinking a module renders UI — it doesn't; it groups components and wires DI.
Forgetting to declare a component in a module, causing 'not a known element' errors.
Putting a component in providers (it's not a service) or a service in declarations.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A component is a UI unit (class + template + styles); a module is an organizer that groups components and wires DI.
Components render; modules don't render — they declare and configure.
Every app has a root module (AppModule) that bootstraps and a root component (AppComponent) that hosts the view.
Declare components in a module; provide services in a module — don't mix them up.
Think 'brick vs box': components are the bricks; modules are the boxes that group them.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: A component and a module are different things in Angular. A component is a reusable UI building block — a TypeScript class with a template and styles that controls a patch of the screen. A module, or NgModule, is an organizational container that groups related components, directives, and services and tells the compiler how to wire dependency injection. The key distinction is that components render UI; modules don't render anything, they organize and configure. Every Angular app has a root module, AppModule, that bootstraps the app, and a root component, AppComponent, that hosts the view tree. A common mistake is thinking a module is a bigger component or that modules render UI — they don't. The analogy is bricks versus boxes: components are the bricks; modules are the boxes that group them and declare which bricks belong together.
